questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Which of the following inequality is true for $x> 0 ?$
questions.solution: Let $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\log (1+\mathrm{x})-\frac{\mathrm{x}}{1+\mathrm{x}}\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad f^{\prime}(\mathrm{x}) &=\frac{1}{1+\mathrm{x}}-\frac{(1+\mathrm{x}) \cdot 1-\mathrm{x} \cdot 1}{(1+\mathrm{x})^{2}} \\ &=\frac{1}{1+\mathrm{x}}-\frac{1}{(1+\mathrm{x})^{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{x}}{(1+\mathrm{x})^{2}} \\ \text { which is positive. } &[\because \mathrm{x}> 0] \end{aligned}\therefore \quad \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ is monotonic increasing, when $\mathrm{x}> 0$. $\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})> \mathrm{f}(0)$ Now, $\mathrm{f}(0)=\log 1-0=0\begin{array}{ll}\therefore & \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})> 0 \\ \Rightarrow & \log (1+\mathrm{x})-\frac{\mathrm{x}}{1+\mathrm{x}}> 0 \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{\mathrm{x}}{1+\mathrm{x}} < \log (1+\mathrm{x}) \\ & \text { Also, for } \mathrm{x}> 0,\end{array} \begin{aligned}$ \text { Also, for }$x>0, \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } x^{2}>0 \Rightarrow x^{2}+x>x \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } x(x+1)>x \\ \text{ and } x>\frac{x}{x+1} \end{aligned}$From eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $\begin{array}{l}\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{x}+1}$< \log (1+\mathrm{x}) < \mathrm{x} \\ {[\because \log (1+x) < \mathrm{x} \text { for } \mathrm{x}>0]} \end{array}

questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \frac{x^{2}+2 x+7}{2 x+3}$< 6 \\
\Rightarrow $\frac{x^{2}+2 x+7}{2 x+3}-$6 < 0 \\
\Rightarrow $\frac{x^{2}-10 x-11}{2 x+3}$< 0 \\
\Rightarrow $\frac{(x-11)(x+1)}{2 x+3}$< 0 \\
\Rightarrow $\frac{(x-11)(x+1)(2 x+3)}{(2 x+3)^{2}}$< 0 \\
\Rightarrow &(x-11)(x+1)(2 x+3) < 0 \\
\Rightarrow & x \in\left(-\infty,$-\frac{3}{2}\right)\cup(-1,11)
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $a, b$ and $c$ are distinct positive numbers, not equal to unity. Such that $a b c=1$, then the value of $\log _b a \cdot \log _c a+\log _c b\cdot \log _a b+\log _a c \log _b c$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \because a b c=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \log a+\log b+\log c=0 \\
& \text { that means, } \\
& \log ^3 a+\log ^3 b+\log ^3 c=3 \log a \cdot \log b \cdot \log c \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\log ^2 a}{\log b \cdot \log c}+\frac{\log ^2 b}{\log a \cdot \log c}+\frac{\log ^2 c}{\log a \cdot \log b}=3 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\log a \cdot \log a}{\log b \cdot \log c}+\frac{\log b \cdot \log b}{\log a \cdot \log c}+\frac{\log c \cdot \log c}{\log a \cdot \log b}=3 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\log _b a}{\log _a c}+\frac{\log _c b}{\log _b a}+\frac{\log _a c}{\log _c b}=3 \\
& \Rightarrow \log _b a \cdot \log _c a+\log _c b \cdot \log _a b \\
& +\log _a c \cdot \log _b c=3
\end{aligned}$
